mainTopic: The ערבה (its two מצוות, the excluded צפצפה, and the חילפא גילא) and the names that switched after the חורבן
overview: The amud opens with אבא שאול, who learns from the plural ״ערבי״ that there are two willow מצוות: one in the לולב and one in the מקדש. The רבנן know the מקדש willow from a הלכה למשה מסיני instead. A ברייתא excludes the צפצפה, a mountain plant, and a verse in יחזקאל is brought to show it is not a water willow. The proof survives a challenge because of the word ״שמו״, explained by רבי אבהו, and the גמרא brings a second version of the same exchange. Another ברייתא gives signs for telling a ערבה from a צפצפה. אביי resolves a contradiction about serrated leaves by explaining it as the חילפא גילא, which is kosher because ״ערבי נחל״ includes every kind of willow. רב חסדא then lists three things whose names swapped after the חורבן, and the גמרא gives a practical difference for each one. אביי adds a pair of stomach compartments, which matters for טריפות. רבא בר יוסף adds the cities בבל and בורסיף, and the question about that pair continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אבא שאול: two willow מצוות
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול learns from the plural ״ערבי״ that there are two willow מצוות, one for the לולב and one for the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: "Willows" (in the plural) means two: one for the לולב, and one for the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול gives his own reading of the plural word ״ערבי״ in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the רבנן used the plural to teach that two willow branches go into the לולב bundle. אבא שאול uses the same plural for something else: one ערבה for the לולב and a separate ערבה מצוה in the מקדש, where it was set around the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argues with the רבנן here
The palm-branch bundle taken on סוכות

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
"Willows" (plural) means two.
One for the lulav,
and one for the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage. It presents an alternative reading of the same plural word the רבנן used earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The plural ״ערבי״ teaches two willow מצוות: one in the לולב and one in the מקדש.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן get the מקדש willow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source the רבנן have for the ערבה of the מקדש, since they used the plural for something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, from where do they know the willow for the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step. If the רבנן did not learn the מקדש-willow from ״ערבי״, where did they learn it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees there was a ערבה מצוה in the מקדש. The רבנן already used the plural to teach two willows in the לולב, so the word is no longer available for the מקדש. That leaves them needing another source.

keyTerms.meaning: "And the Rabbis": introduces a question about the other opinion

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, from where do they know the willow for the Temple?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אבא שאול by asking how the other side accounts for the same law.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the מקדש-willow according to the רבנן.

steps.title: It is a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן know the מקדש-willow from a הלכה למשה מסיני. רבי יוחנן lists it with עשר נטיעות and ניסוך המים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learned it as a tradition. As רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: עשר נטיעות, the ערבה, and ניסוך המים are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן do not need a פסוק. The ערבה of the מקדש is an oral tradition going back to משה at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הלכה למשה מסיני is a law handed down orally, with no source in the written verses. רבי יוחנן names three such laws: plowing around ten saplings before שביעית, the ערבה in the מקדש, and pouring water on the מזבח on סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: A law given orally to משה at סיני, without a verse
Ten saplings: a field may be plowed for them right up to שביעית
Pouring water on the מזבח during סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: אבא שאול learns the מקדש-willow from the plural ״ערבי״. The רבנן know it from a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן agree there is a ערבה in the מקדש. They only disagree with אבא שאול about where the law comes from.

phrases.english: They learned it as a tradition.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation —
are a law given to Moshe at Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מקדש-willow is a הלכה למשה מסיני, supported by רבי יוחנן's list of three laws.

steps.title: ברייתא: ״ערבי נחל״ excludes the צפצפה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that ״ערבי נחל״ means willows that grow by a river, which rules out the צפצפה that grows in the mountains.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: ״ערבי נחל״ means those that grow by the river. This excludes the צפצפה, which grows among the mountains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that defines which kind of willow is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word נחל tells us the kosher ערבה is the kind that grows by water. The צפצפה looks similar but grows in the mountains, so it is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: A willow-like plant that is not kosher for the מצוה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "Willows of the brook" —
those that grow by the river,
to exclude the tzaftzafa, which grows among the mountains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: which plant counts as a kosher ערבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only willows that grow by water are kosher. The mountain צפצפה is excluded.

steps.title: רבי זירא's verse: the צפצפה does not grow by water
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a פסוק from יחזקאל showing that a צפצפה is not a water plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: What is the verse? "He placed it by great waters, he set it as a צפצפה."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a verse to prove that a צפצפה is different from a plant that grows by water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as describing a change. Something was planted by great waters and then turned into a צפצפה. That suggests a צפצפה is not the plant that grows by water.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: What is the verse?
"He placed it by great waters,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in יחזקאל 17:5.

phrases.english: he set it as a tzaftzafa."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a verse that supports the ברייתא's distinction.
steps.raayaObject: That the צפצפה is not a water-growing willow.

steps.title: אביי: maybe the verse calls the water plant a צפצפה
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests the second half of the פסוק simply explains the first, so the plant by the water would itself be a צפצפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Perhaps the verse is just explaining. "He placed it by great waters," and what is it? A צפצפה!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבי זירא's proof by offering a different way to read the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״צפצפה״ is just naming the plant that was by the water, then the verse proves the opposite: a צפצפה does grow by water. On that reading, רבי זירא's proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who challenges רבי זירא

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And perhaps it is just explaining:
"He placed it by great waters,"
and what is it? A tzaftzafa!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's reading of the verse.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the verse, not the ברייתא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse could be naming the water plant, rather than describing a change into a צפצפה.

steps.title: The word 'set it' shows a change
steps.stepSummary: The reply: if the verse were only explaining, the word ״שמו״ would be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does "set it" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא's reading is defended by pointing to the extra word ״שמו״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״שמו״, "he set it / made it," shows that something changed. The plant started as a water willow and was turned into a צפצפה. That brings back the original proof.

phrases.english: If so, what does "set it" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse merely names the water plant as a צפצפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״שמו״ signals a transformation, so the צפצפה is different from the water willow.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: ישראל was meant to be a ערבה but became a צפצפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains the פסוק: הקב״ה wanted ישראל to be like a willow by the water, but they made themselves like a mountain צפצפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: הקב״ה said: I wanted ישראל to be before Me like a plant placed by great waters, which is the ערבה. But they made themselves like the צפצפה of the mountains.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו's teaching backs up the reading that the verse describes a change from willow to צפצפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אבהו's reading, the plant by the water is the ערבה, and the mountain plant is the צפצפה. So the two are different plants, which confirms the ברייתא. The verse is also a rebuke: ישראל lowered themselves from their intended place.
steps.whatToRemember: The kosher ערבה grows by water. The צפצפה grows in the mountains and is excluded. The word ״שמו״ in יחזקאל shows they are two different plants.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I said that Israel should be before Me
like "placed by great waters,"
and what is that? The willow.
But they made themselves
like the tzaftzafa of the mountains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 7 with an authoritative reading of the verse.
steps.raayaObject: That the verse contrasts the water-growing willow with the mountain צפצפה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ערבה and the צפצפה are different plants, so the צפצפה is not kosher for the מצוה.

steps.title: Another version: the verse is part of the teaching itself
steps.stepSummary: Some versions place the פסוק ״קח על מים רבים צפצפה שמו״ inside the ברייתא as its own source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach this verse as part of the ברייתא: "He placed it by great waters, he set it as a צפצפה."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second version of the discussion we just learned. In this version, the ברייתא itself quotes the פסוק as its proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבי זירא brought the פסוק to support the ברייתא, and אביי challenged it. In this version, the פסוק is already inside the ברייתא. So the person who challenges it changes, as the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: On the ברייתא (as part of it)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is the same exchange from steps 5-8, retold with different attribution.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it
this verse as part of the baraita:
"He placed it by great waters,
he set it as a tzaftzafa."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהַאי קְרָא אַמַּתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the proof of step 5 as part of the ברייתא itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's own source that a צפצפה is not a water plant is the פסוק in יחזקאל.

steps.title: רבי זירא challenges the reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests the פסוק may just be explaining which plant grew by the water, namely a צפצפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objects: Maybe the verse is just explaining itself: "He placed it by great waters." What was it? A צפצפה!
steps.whatsHappening: In this version, רבי זירא is the one who attacks the proof. He says the פסוק might be calling the water plant a צפצפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same challenge אביי made in step 6. If the second half of the פסוק only explains the first half, then a צפצפה does grow by water. That would ruin the proof that a צפצפה is a mountain plant.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to it:
But perhaps it is merely explaining:
"He placed it by great waters" —
what is it? A tzaftzafa!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof inside the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of the פסוק to exclude צפצפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second half of the פסוק may just name the water plant, which would make the צפצפה a water plant.

steps.title: The word "set it" defeats the challenge
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק were only explaining, the word ״שמו״ would add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does "he set it" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי זירא's challenge. The extra word ״שמו״ shows the פסוק is describing a change, not giving an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״שמו״ means "he made it into." That word implies something was turned from one thing into another. So the water plant (a ערבה) was turned into a צפצפה, which means the two are different plants.

keyTerms.meaning: He set it / made it into

phrases.english: If so, what is the meaning of "he set it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: an extra word proves the reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק simply identifies the water plant as a צפצפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״שמו״ shows a change from a water plant into a צפצפה, so they are different plants.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's explanation of the verse, repeated
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains: הקב״ה wanted ישראל to be like a willow by water, but they made themselves like a mountain צפצפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: הקב״ה said, "I wanted ישראל to be before Me like a plant by great waters, which is a ערבה. But they made themselves like a צפצפה of the mountains."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי אבהו's explanation as the ending of this second version. It confirms the reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's reading separates the two plants. The water plant is the ערבה, and the צפצפה is a mountain plant. That confirms the ברייתא's point that a צפצפה is not "ערבי נחל".

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I said that Israel should be before Me
like "placed by great waters" —
and what is that? A willow;
but they set themselves
as a tzaftzafa of the mountains.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 11 with a full reading of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That the water plant (ערבה) and the צפצפה are different
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבהו's explanation of the פסוק in יחזקאל
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the conclusion is the same: a צפצפה is a mountain tree, not a ערבה, so it is not valid.

steps.title: How to tell a ערבה from a צפצפה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the signs. A ערבה has a red stem, a long leaf, and a smooth edge. A צפצפה has a white stem, a round leaf, and an edge like a sickle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: What is a ערבה and what is a צפצפה? A ערבה has a red stem, a long leaf, and a smooth edge. A צפצפה has a white stem, a round leaf, and an edge with teeth like a sickle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with practical signs for telling the kosher ערבה apart from the invalid צפצפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know a צפצפה is invalid, we need a way to recognize it. The ברייתא gives three signs: stem color, leaf shape, and leaf edge.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
What is a willow and what is a tzaftzafa?
A willow: its stem is red,
its leaf is elongated,
and its edge is smooth.
A tzaftzafa: its stem is white,
its leaf is round,
and its edge resembles a sickle.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵי זֶהוּ עֲרָבָה וְאֵיזֶהוּ צַפְצָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source that excludes צפצפה to practical signs for identifying it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערבה has a red stem, a long leaf, and a smooth edge. A צפצפה has a white stem, a round leaf, and a sickle-like edge.

steps.title: Another teaching says a sickle-edged willow is kosher
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא says a leaf with a sickle-like edge is kosher and only a saw-like edge is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another ברייתא teaches: if the edge is like a sickle, it is kosher. If it is like a saw, it is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. One ברייתא calls a sickle edge the sign of a צפצפה, but another ברייתא says a sickle-edged willow is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא implies that a ערבה always has a smooth edge. The other ברייתא assumes there is a valid ערבה with a sickle-like edge. Both cannot be fully true as stated.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
if it resembles a sickle, it is fit;
if it resembles a saw, it is unfit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 13 using another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sign that a sickle-like edge means צפצפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא calls a sickle-edged willow kosher, so a sickle edge cannot be the mark of the invalid צפצפה.

steps.title: אביי: that teaching is about the חילפא גילא
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the second ברייתא is talking about a special type of willow, the חילפא גילא, whose leaves are serrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That ברייתא is talking about a חילפא גילא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. The two ברייתות are talking about different plants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary willows have smooth edges, as our ברייתא says. But one specific kind of willow, the חילפא גילא, naturally has sickle-like edges. It is still a real ערבה, so the other ברייתא calls it kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: A specific type of willow with serrated leaves

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When that baraita was taught,
it was referring to ḥilfa gila.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות speak about the same ordinary willow and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא that allows a sickle edge refers only to the חילפא גילא, a willow that naturally has serrated leaves.

steps.title: אביי concludes: חילפא גילא is kosher
steps.stepSummary: From his answer, אביי concludes that a חילפא גילא is kosher for the four species.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that a חילפא גילא is kosher for the הושענא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a practical ruling from the answer he just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא called a sickle-edged willow kosher, and אביי explained that it means the חילפא גילא. So it follows directly that a חילפא גילא may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: The bundle of the four species (here, for the ערבה)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Conclude from it that this ḥilfa gila
is fit for the hoshana.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a ruling from אביי's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חילפא גילא is kosher for the ערבה of the four species.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why אביי needed to say this, since it already follows from the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's ruling as unnecessary. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ברייתא calls it kosher, stating it again seems to add nothing new. The גמרא expects every statement to teach something.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why אביי's ruling was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's statement that חילפא גילא is kosher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It already follows from the ברייתא, so stating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The extra name might have made it invalid
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that because it has a describing word added to its name, it is not a real ערבה. אביי teaches that it is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since its name has an extra describing word, it is not kosher. So אביי teaches us that it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point in אביי's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a species with an added describing word in its name (שם לווי) is not the plain species. אביי teaches that this rule does not disqualify חילפא גילא, even though it is called "חילפא גילא" and not just "חילפא".
steps.whyThisMatters: שם לווי is a concept that disqualifies plants elsewhere, for example certain kinds of אזוב. Here the plural ״ערבי נחל״ shows that it does not disqualify a willow.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
since it has a modifier in its name,
it should not be fit;
he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the statement removes a possible mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A plant with a שם לווי is not considered a real ערבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חילפא גילא is kosher despite its שם לווי.

steps.title: Maybe it really should be invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not accept that the extra name does make it invalid?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it really is so, and it is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and asks why the reasoning of the הוה אמינא is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern about שם לווי seemed reasonable. So the גמרא wants a source showing that it does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: And say it is indeed so

phrases.english: And say it is indeed so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that חילפא גילא is kosher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שם לווי reasoning seems sound, so maybe it should be invalid.

steps.title: "Willows of the brook" includes every kind of willow
steps.stepSummary: The תורה says ״ערבי נחל״ in the plural, which includes every kind of willow.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה said "ערבי נחל" (willows of the brook, in plural), meaning any kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the פסוק and closes the discussion: a חילפא גילא is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word ״ערבי״ shows the תורה includes more than one kind of willow. So even a willow with an added describing name, like חילפא גילא, counts as kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case / of any kind

steps.whatToRemember: A צפצפה (white stem, round leaf) is invalid. Any real willow is kosher, including the serrated חילפא גילא, because ״ערבי נחל״ is plural.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said "willows of the brook" —
in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַרְבֵי נַחַל אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא מִכׇּל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 with a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The plural ״ערבי נחל״ includes every kind of willow, so a חילפא גילא is kosher despite its שם לווי.

steps.title: רב חסדא: three items swapped names, starting with the two kinds of willow
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that after the חורבן, three things switched names. The first pair is חלפתא and ערבתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: These three items had their names switched once the בית המקדש was destroyed. What used to be called ערבתא is now called חלפתא, and what used to be called חלפתא is now called ערבתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא opens a list of three name-swaps. Here he gives the first one: the two kinds of willow traded names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects directly to the earlier discussion about which willow is kosher for the ארבעה מינים. If people now use the old names in reverse, someone looking for a kosher ערבה could easily end up with the wrong plant. רב חסדא is warning us that the words people use today do not match the words used in the original sources.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of willow (the name now used for the plant once called ערבה)
Willow (the ערבה; its name has swapped with חלפתא)
From the time the בית המקדש was destroyed

steps.confusionAlert: The items themselves did not change. Only the NAMES people use switched places. The plant that is kosher for the ערבה is the same plant as always; people just call it by the other name now.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
These three items had their names changed
from when the Temple was destroyed:
'chalafta' is now what was 'aravta' (willow),
and 'aravta' is now what was 'chalafta'.
phrases.notes: The two names simply traded places.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָנֵי תְּלָת מִילֵּי אִשְׁתַּנִּי שְׁמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the discussion of which willow is a valid ערבה by noting that the names of the willow types have themselves switched.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the חורבן, the names ערבתא and חלפתא swapped places (the first of three such swaps).

steps.title: What practical difference does the willow name-swap make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it matters that the willow names switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does this make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. It wants to know the practical result of the willow name-switch, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is not challenging רב חסדא. It is asking why this piece of word history matters in real life. This becomes a pattern: after each name-swap, the גמרא asks the same question.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference comes out of it?

phrases.english: What practical difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical importance of the name-swap just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result of knowing that the willow names switched.

steps.title: It matters for the מצוה of לולב
steps.stepSummary: The difference is for the לולב: one must take the right willow even though it now goes by the other name.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the name-swap matters for the מצוה of לולב and the ארבעה מינים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone buying a ערבה for סוכות needs the plant the תורה calls ערבה. Since that plant is now called חלפתא, asking for 'ערבתא' by today's name would get him the wrong one. Knowing the switch protects the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The palm branch; here it stands for the whole set of ארבעה מינים, including the ערבה

phrases.english: For the lulav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The willow name-swap matters for the מצוה of לולב: one must take the plant that is truly a ערבה, even though it now goes by the other name.

steps.title: Second swap: שופר and trumpet
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's second pair: the names שיפורא (shofar) and חצוצרתא (trumpet) switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: What used to be called a שופר is now called a חצוצרתא (trumpet), and what used to be called a חצוצרתא is now called a שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רב חסדא's list with the second item: the words for שופר and trumpet traded places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of switch as the willows. The ram's horn (the real שופר) is now commonly called a 'trumpet', and the metal trumpet is now called a 'shofar'.

phrases.english: 'Shofar' is now what was 'trumpet',
and 'trumpet' is now what was 'shofar'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in רב חסדא's list of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names שופר and חצוצרה swapped after the חורבן.

steps.title: What practical difference does the שופר swap make?
steps.stepSummary: Same question again: why does the שופר/trumpet switch matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does this make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its question for the second pair. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is consistent. Each name-swap must have a real-life halachic result, or there would be no reason to record it.

keyTerms.meaning: Ram's horn used on ראש השנה

phrases.english: What practical difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical importance of the second swap.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result of the שופר/trumpet name-switch.

steps.title: It matters for the שופר of ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: The difference is for blowing שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for the שופר of ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this switch matters for the מצוה of blowing שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ראש השנה one must blow a real ram's horn. Since that horn is now called a 'trumpet', a person who asks what to use should be told to bring what people today call a 'trumpet', not what they now call a 'shofar'.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year, when the מצוה is to blow a שופר

phrases.english: For the shofar of Rosh Hashanah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For the שופר of ראש השנה, one must use the real ram's horn, which is now called by the 'trumpet' name.

steps.title: Third swap: small table and large table
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's third pair: פתורתא (small table) and פתורא (large table) switched names.
steps.simpleTranslation: What used to be called a פתורתא (small table) is now called a פתורא, and what used to be called a פתורא (large table) is now called a פתורתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third and last item on רב חסדא's list: the words for a small table and a large table traded places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first two, this pair has nothing to do with a מצוה object. It is an everyday household item, which shows that name-swaps can affect ordinary business too.

phrases.english: 'Petorata' (small table) is now called 'petora',
and 'petora' (large table) is now called 'petorata'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final item in רב חסדא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names for a small table and a large table swapped after the חורבן.

steps.title: What practical difference does the table swap make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the table name-switch matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what practical matter does this make a difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks its question a third time. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the wording is slightly different ('לְמַאי', meaning 'for what'), but the function is the same. The גמרא wants a real-life consequence.

phrases.english: For what does it make a practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical importance of the third swap.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result of the table name-switch.

steps.title: It matters for buying and selling
steps.stepSummary: The difference is in business deals: a sale is understood according to the names people use now.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for buying and selling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the table switch matters for business deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone orders or sells a 'פתורא', we must know which size table that word means today. The deal is understood by current speech, so a buyer who says 'פתורא' now gets the small table.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's three swaps each carry a practical result: the willows matter for לולב, the שופר/trumpet matters for ראש השנה, and the tables matter for business deals. Words in halacha must be understood the way people use them in their own time.

phrases.english: For buying and selling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28 and completes רב חסדא's list.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The table switch matters for transactions: a sale is interpreted according to the current names.

steps.title: אביי adds a fourth swap: two parts of the animal's stomach
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds his own example: the names בי כסי and הובלילא, two stomach compartments of a cud-chewing animal, have switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I too say there is such a switch. What used to be called הובלילא is now called בי כסי, and what used to be called בי כסי is now called הובלילא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues רב חסדא's theme and adds another pair of names that traded places in his own time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are two neighboring compartments of a ruminant's stomach. As with רב חסדא's pairs, the גמרא will next ask what practical difference this switch makes. Steps 31-32 answer that it matters for a needle found in the wall of בית הכוסות, a question of טריפות.

keyTerms.meaning: I too say (adding to the previous teaching)
An inner compartment of a cud-chewing animal's stomach (בית הכוסות)
Another stomach compartment, next to בית הכוסות

phrases.english: Abaye said: I too say:
'Bei kasei' is now what was 'huvlila',
and 'huvlila' is now what was 'bei kasei'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי extends רב חסדא's list with a further example of the same phenomenon.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names of two stomach compartments, הובלילא and בי כסי, have swapped.

steps.title: Why does the stomach-compartment name switch matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference comes out of אביי's point that the names of the two stomach compartments switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks its usual question: why should we care that the names of the two stomach parts switched? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא asks this same question after every name-switch in this list. A name change is only worth recording if it changes how we act. Here it asks that question about אביי's example of בי כסי and הובלילא.

keyTerms.meaning: Practical difference; what comes out of it in real life or in הלכה
An Aramaic name for one of the stomach compartments of a cud-chewing animal
An Aramaic name for another stomach compartment, which switched names with בי כסי

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
phrases.notes: This same question gets asked after each name-switch in this list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical importance of אביי's name-switch from step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What halachic difference results from the switch between the names בי כסי and הובלילא.

steps.title: It matters for a needle found in the stomach wall
steps.stepSummary: The difference concerns a needle found inside the thick wall of בית הכוסות. Whether the animal is a טרפה depends on which compartment it is in, so the correct name matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for a needle that is found in the thickness of the wall of בית הכוסות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the name-switch matters for a needle found stuck in the wall of a stomach compartment. Knowing exactly which compartment it is affects whether the animal is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of טרפה, a needle stuck in the wall of בית הכוסות from only one side does not make the animal a טרפה. If it shows through on both sides, the animal is a טרפה. In the other compartment, even a one-sided puncture makes the animal a טרפה, so mixing up the names could lead to a wrong ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Thickness; here, the thick wall of the stomach
The second stomach compartment of a cud-chewing animal, with a honeycomb-like wall
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten even after proper שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume a needle in any part of the stomach has the same rule. In בית הכוסות a one-sided puncture does not make the animal a טרפה, but in the other compartment it does. That difference is the whole reason the names matter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a change in everyday language can affect a real kashrus question. A שוחט or a רב has to know which organ people mean by each name.

phrases.english: For a needle that is found in the thickness of the wall of the second stomach compartment.
phrases.notes: The rule for a needle depends on which compartment it is in, so the correct name matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The name-switch affects the טרפה ruling for a needle found in the wall of בית הכוסות, because the rule differs between the two compartments.

steps.title: רבא בר יוסף adds: בבל and בורסיף switched names
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר יוסף adds his own example: the cities בבל and בורסיף switched names.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר יוסף said: I too say that the place once called בבל is now called בורסיף, and the place once called בורסיף is now called בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא joins the list of name-switches. רבא בר יוסף says the names of two cities, בבל and בורסיף, got swapped over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'I too say' show he is adding to the list started by רב חסדא and continued by אביי. This time the switch is between place names, not objects or body parts. The גמרא will next ask why this matters.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who adds another example of switched names
'I too say', used when adding one's own example to a list others started

phrases.english: Rava bar Yosef said:
I too say:
phrases.notes: He's adding one more name-switch to the list.

phrases.english: Babylon is now called Bursif,
and Bursif is now called Babylon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר יוֹסֵף, אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another name-switch to the list, following אביי's example in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names of the cities בבל and בורסיף have switched.

steps.title: The question begins: why does the city-name switch matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its usual question about what practical difference the בבל and בורסיף switch makes. The question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what...?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins asking what practical difference the city-name switch makes. Only the first word appears here, and the rest of the question and its answer come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same pattern as the earlier examples: a name-switch is followed by 'what difference does it make?'. The question is cut off at the end of the amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For what?', the opening word of the question about a practical difference

phrases.english: For what...
phrases.notes: The question is cut off here and continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins asking for the practical importance of רבא בר יוסף's statement in step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What halachic difference results from the switch between the names בבל and בורסיף (the question continues on the next amud).
